references.text: Even earlier, the disciples did not understand Jesus' words about his suffering: "But they did not understand this saying; it was hidden from them, so that they might not grasp it" ([ref:Luk 9:45|Luke 9:45]). An almost identical formulation shows that this was a recurring problem for the disciples.

Even as a child, Jesus said things that those closest to him did not understand: "But they did not understand what he said to them" ([ref:Luk 2:50|Luke 2:50]). Luke uses this motif of lack of understanding throughout his gospel.

Mark reports the same about the disciples' lack of understanding after Jesus' second prediction of his suffering: "But they did not understand this saying and were afraid to ask him" ([ref:Mark 9:32|Mark 9:32]).

Jesus rebuked the disciples for their lack of understanding: "Do you still not understand or perceive? Is your heart hardened?" ([ref:Mark 8:17|Mark 8:17]). The disciples' foolishness is a central theme in the Gospel of Mark.

John also tells us that the disciples did not at first understand what happened: "His disciples did not understand these things at first. But when Jesus had been glorified, they remembered that these things were written about him" ([ref:Joh 12:16|John 12:16]). Understanding came only after the resurrection.
Even at the empty tomb, the disciples still had not understood what the Scripture says: "For as yet they did not understand the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead" ([ref:Joh 20:9|John 20:9]).

After the resurrection, Jesus opened the disciples' understanding by explaining the Scriptures: "O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!" ([ref:Luk 24:25-27|Luke 24:25-27]). What had been hidden was now revealed.
Jesus "opened their minds so they could understand the Scriptures" ([ref:Luk 24:45-46|Luke 24:45-46]). This is the direct resolution of the lack of understanding described in Luke 18:34.

Paul writes that a veil lies over the mind when the Law of Moses is read, but "when one turns to the Lord, the veil is removed" ([ref:2 Kor 3:14-16|2 Corinthians 3:14-16]). The idea that truth can be "hidden" until God reveals it is parallel.

Isaiah's prophecy about the people's spiritual blindness: "Hear and hear, but do not understand! See and see, but do not perceive!" ([ref:Jes 6:9-10|Isaiah 6:9-10]). The disciples' lack of understanding belongs to the broader biblical motif of spiritual blindness.
